stages.name: Data processing
stages.definition: Acquiring, extracting, cleaning, restructuring, or computing data before visual encoding. Selecting a subset within an existing view alone does not qualify.

stages.name: Visual mapping
stages.definition: Creating or revising mappings from data to marks, channels, or chart structures. Inspecting or annotating a chart alone does not qualify.

stages.name: View transformation
stages.definition: Changing the focus, subset, granularity, arrangement, or navigational state of a view for exploration. Producing a new encoding is visual mapping instead.

stages.name: Presentation
stages.definition: Externalizing an interpretation through explanatory text, annotations, summaries, or reports. Merely displaying or exporting a chart, or authoring a question about one, does not qualify.

modes.name: Guiding
modes.definition: Providing a goal, prompt, example, constraint, or selected input context for the model’s next output. The user does not directly edit a model-produced artifact in this action.

modes.name: Selecting or rating
modes.definition: Choosing, accepting, rejecting, or evaluating a model-produced candidate or suggestion. Selecting source data or navigating a view is insufficient.

modes.name: Post-editing
modes.definition: Directly changing a model-produced artifact, with the edit remaining local or final rather than becoming input for model continuation. Asking the model to make the change is guiding.

modes.name: Interactive editing
modes.definition: Directly revising a model-produced draft or identified part, after which the system feeds that revision to the model and the model continues or regenerates from it. A new question or retry without editing the draft is insufficient.

modes.name: User-led presentation authoring
modes.definition: Retaining authorship of an analytic explanation, report, dashboard text, data story, or text–visual account while the model suggests or continues material. An automatically drafted report without user-led composition is excluded. U applies only to PR.

rules: The crosswalk records documented active intervention targeting an LLM-related artifact, rather than all capabilities reported by a system.
An action is assigned only to the stage it directly targets; an automatic downstream result does not inherit the action’s mode.
A paper contributes at most once to a stage–mode cell. Distinct documented actions may place a paper in multiple cells.
Stage and mode totals count distinct papers. They are not sums of the corresponding cells.
U outside PR is structurally inapplicable (NA), rather than an observed zero.
An empty crosswalk field means no matching action is recorded. It does not prove a capability is absent from the implementation.
Evidence strings are supplied coding summaries, not verbatim quotations. Section/page locators are not supplied in the source CSV.
The explorer uses consensus labels; independent coder labels are not available here and agreement coefficients are not recalculated.
